title: Modi Heads to Manila for ASEAN and East Asia Summits From November 16 to 18
excerpt: The Prime Minister will attend the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit in the Philippine capital, with bilateral meetings and an Indian community interaction also planned.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Manila from November 16 to 18 for the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit, India's foreign ministry said on Thursday.
  • The Philippines, this year's ASEAN chair, is hosting the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits under the theme "Navigating the Future," with at least 19 world and global institution leaders expected.
  • Modi's programme includes a dinner hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., bilateral meetings with other leaders, and a planned interaction with the Indian community in the Philippines.
  • The MEA put two-way trade with ASEAN at USD 122 billion, calling the bloc a major trading partner for India.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will travel to the Philippines from November 16 to 18 to attend the summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in Manila, India's foreign ministry said on Thursday, according to Reuters. India is a strategic partner of the 11-member grouping, which consists of Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia, and Timor-Leste.

What Is on the Programme

Briefing reporters in New Delhi on November 12, MEA Secretary (East) Tandon said Modi will attend the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st meeting of the ASEAN-led East Asia Summit process. The Prime Minister will attend a dinner hosted by President Marcos for the visiting dignitaries a day before the two summits, and his schedule also includes bilateral meetings with other leaders on the sidelines. An interaction with members of the Indian community in the Philippines is being planned as part of the visit.

The Philippines is chairing this year's ASEAN process, and Manila will host the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits. The theme of this year's summit and related meetings is "Navigating the Future." The Philippines will host at least 19 world and global institution leaders for the meetings.

Why ASEAN Matters to India

India's engagement with ASEAN sits at the centre of its Act East policy. Ahead of the visit, Tandon described ASEAN as "a major trading partner" for India, putting two-way trade at USD 122 billion, according to ANI's report of the briefing. The East Asia Summit, which brings ASEAN together with partners including India, the United States, China, Japan, and Australia, is the region's main leaders-led forum for strategic and security questions.

A wider leaders' gathering may also take shape on the sidelines. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on October 20 that the United States, India, Japan, and Australia had agreed to hold their next Quad leaders' summit in Manila alongside the ASEAN meetings, which would be the grouping's first leaders' summit since September 21, 2024. The precise date, format, and participant list for that meeting await final confirmation, and arrangements depend on US President Donald Trump's attendance.

What Happens Next

The visit runs from Monday, November 16 to Wednesday, November 18; the Philippine government has declared those three days special non-working days across the National Capital Region for the summit. The ASEAN-India Summit is where leaders take stock of the partnership and set its direction for the coming year, while the East Asia Summit a day later puts Modi in the room with the region's other major powers. Any announcements on trade, maritime cooperation, or connectivity will come out of those sessions.
